g.text: D22 — recency-rollup-index (one index on an aggregate D4 already stores)
all D4 columns and indexes, plus ONE line:
D4 already MAINTAINS last_donation_at on every write —
q06 already reads it, per-person. What it never had is
a GLOBAL access path: person_last_donation_idx is
charity, and q13/q14/q16 (RECENCY.md) ask across all of
This is the whole design: one index, zero new
maintenance. Compare against D20 (a flag materialised
on the CHILD, with its own trigger and write cost) —
see the D20 -> D22 pair in RECENCY.md section 4.
d23_recency_rollup_app_idx is the same one-line index,
on D5's APPLICATION-maintained rollup instead of D4's
trigger — reads byte-identical, so any measured
difference between D22 and D23 is the concurrency
strategy (trigger vs application), not the SQL.
